title: Image-based 3D Cell Culture Cytotoxicity Assay
author: Elinor Gottschalk
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.72shqee

steps.title: Culture and activate T cells
steps.instruction: If using T cells, start culturing them, activate, maintain in appropriate media, supplement as needed, and split until the day of co‑culture.

steps.title: Prepare MC38 spheroids (day before)
steps.instruction: Make a single‑cell suspension of MC38 cells at 2.5 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹ in DMEM with 10 % FBS and 1 % pen/strep. Using a multichannel pipettor, dispense five rows of 20 µl droplets (40 droplets total) onto the inner surface of a 10 cm tissue‑culture dish lid. Add 5–10 ml sterile water to the bottom half of the dish to humidify the chamber. Carefully invert the lid over the water‑filled bottom (avoid bumping the lid to prevent droplet flattening). Incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

substeps.instruction: Make MC38 single‑cell suspension (2.5 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹ in DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % pen/strep).
Pipette 5 rows × 20 µl droplets (40 droplets) onto inner lid surface.
Add 5–10 ml sterile water to dish bottom to humidify.
Invert lid over water without disturbing droplets.
Incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ overnight.

steps.title: Harvest and filter spheroids
steps.instruction: In the hood, flip the lid to expose droplets (an empty dish bottom can be placed on top for microscopy). Harvest spheroids with a P1000 using 2 ml DMEM per lid and transfer to a 50 ml tube. Pass the suspension through a 40 µm nylon mesh filter, invert the filter over a new 50 ml tube and wash retained spheroids into the tube. Then pass the suspension through a 100 µm filter into another 50 ml tube (collect flow‑through). Centrifuge the combined spheroid suspension at 200 × g for 5 min.

substeps.instruction: Flip lid in hood, check spheroid formation on inverted microscope.
Harvest spheroids with P1000 + 2 ml DMEM per lid; transfer to 50 ml tube.
Filter through 40 µm nylon mesh.
Invert 40 µm filter over new tube and wash retained spheroids into tube.
Filter the suspension through 100 µm filter into another tube (collect flow‑through).
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min.

steps.title: Prepare collagen gel on ice
steps.instruction: While the spheroid pellet is centrifuging, keep all steps on ice in the hood. In a sterile Eppendorf tube, mix the listed collagen‑gel components by pipetting up and down, avoiding air bubbles, until the phenol‑red color is uniform. Check pH: the solution should appear red. If slightly yellow, add 0.5 M NaOH in 1 µl increments, mixing each time, until red; if it turns purple, restart the mix.

substeps.instruction: Mix collagen‑gel components on ice in sterile tube, pipette to avoid bubbles.
Mix until phenol‑red color is uniform.
Adjust pH: add 0.5 M NaOH 1 µl increments if yellow; restart if purple.

steps.title: Embed spheroids in collagen and seed chips
steps.instruction: Aspirate as much DMEM as possible from the spheroid pellet. Resuspend the pellet in the prepared collagen mix. Test spheroid density by pipetting a 10 µl droplet onto a dish and inspecting under a microscope; add more gel if too dense (≈50 µl gel per 10 cm dish worth of spheroids works well). Pipette 10 µl of gel into each chip’s central channel slowly: fill the top port until the gel reaches halfway, then fill the bottom port until the channel is full. If using AIM Biotech chip holders, add sterile water to the chambers to keep chips humidified. Incubate the seeded chips at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 30 min to polymerize the gel.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate DMEM from spheroid pellet as completely as possible.
Resuspend pellet in collagen mix.
Assess density with 10 µl droplet; add extra gel if needed (≈50 µl per 10 cm dish).
Pipette 10 µl gel into central channel: top port to halfway, then bottom port to fill.
If using AIM Biotech holders, add sterile water to humidify chambers.
Incubate chips 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 30 min for polymerization.

steps.title: Prepare T cells or drug dilutions
steps.instruction: For T cells: count and harvest the desired number, optionally stain with a live‑cell marker, centrifuge at 350 × g for 5 min, and resuspend in T‑cell media supplemented with IL‑2 (200 IU ml⁻¹) to the required concentration (serial dilutions from a maximum of 4 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹). For Staurosporine treatment: dilute the Staurosporine stock into DMEM containing 10 % FBS and 1 % pen/strep to the desired concentrations.

substeps.instruction: T‑cell preparation: count, harvest, optional staining.
Centrifuge T cells 350 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend in media + IL‑2 (200 IU ml⁻¹); make serial dilutions from 4 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹.
Staurosporine preparation: dilute stock in DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % pen/strep to desired concentrations.

steps.title: Add T cells or drug to chips
steps.instruction: Remove chips from the incubator and place them in the hood. For T‑cell co‑culture: pipette 20 µl of T‑cell media (IL‑2 200 IU ml⁻¹) with or without hgp100 peptide (2 µM) into the top port of the right side channel of each channel, then add 50 µl of the same media to both the top and bottom ports of that side channel. Pipette 20 µl of the T‑cell suspension into the left side channel (mix the suspension before each addition) and do not top‑off this side to avoid displacing cells. For Staurosporine‑treated samples: pipette 20 µl of the Staurosporine‑DMEM solution into both left and right side channels, then top‑off all four side‑channel ports with 50 µl of the same media. Return the chips to humidified holders and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

substeps.instruction: Place chips in hood.
T‑cell condition: 20 µl IL‑2 media ± hgp100 peptide (2 µM) into top port of right side channel.
Add 50 µl same media to top and bottom ports of right side channel.
Add 20 µl T‑cell suspension into left side channel (mix before each addition); do not top‑off left side.
Staurosporine condition: 20 µl Staurosporine‑DMEM into left and right side channels.
Top‑off all four side‑channel ports with 50 µl same media.
Return chips to humidified holders; incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Stain chips for imaging
steps.instruction: Prepare staining solution: 5 ml PBS, 20 drops NucBlue, and 18 µl SYTOX Red dead‑cell stain. For each chip, first remove any media from the troughs around the side‑channel ports (do not aspirate directly from the ports). Gently pipette 20 µl of the staining buffer into the top port of each side channel, allowing it to push existing media/T cells out the bottom port. Remove any residual media from the bottom‑port troughs, then gently pipette 50 µl of the stain into the top port of each side channel until it exits the bottom port. Incubate the chip for 30 min at room temperature protected from light.

substeps.instruction: Make staining solution: 5 ml PBS + 20 drops NucBlue + 18 µl SYTOX Red.
Remove media from troughs around side‑channel ports (do not aspirate from ports).
Pipette 20 µl staining buffer into top port of each side channel; watch it push out contents.
Remove media from bottom‑port troughs.
Pipette 50 µl stain into top port of each side channel until it exits bottom port.
Incubate 30 min at room temperature, protected from light.

steps.title: Acquire images of chips
steps.instruction: Set microscope exposure using the Staurosporine‑treated positive‑control chip: CH1 = Cy5 (SYTOX Red) – image this channel first because SYTOX photobleaches after DAPI; CH2 = DAPI; CH3 = brightfield. Apply the same settings to all chips. Define a 3 × 11 grid per channel with multipoint acquisition for the three channels. Use the high‑resolution setting (optional). Image each chip (≈30 min per chip). While one chip is imaging, begin staining the next chip to keep staining times consistent across samples.

substeps.instruction: Set exposure based on Staurosporine control: CH1 = Cy5 (SYTOX Red) first, CH2 = DAPI, CH3 = brightfield.
Apply identical settings to all chips.
Create 3 × 11 grid per channel with multipoint acquisition.
Select high‑resolution mode (optional).
Image each chip (~30 min).
During imaging, start staining the next chip to maintain consistent staining times.

steps.title: Analyze images (optional)
steps.instruction: Analyze the acquired images with Cytokit (https://github.com/hammerlab/cytokit) following the methods described by Czech et al., 2019.
